candidate_analysis.explanation: The Random Forest predicts MALWARE with probability 0.96, and all 20 top n-grams push toward cryptojacking. However, the evidence does not name any functions, API calls, or strings, and the per-feature SHAP values are small and evenly spread (+0.0047 to +0.0096), so no single feature is decisive. Several n-grams are consistent with the bit-rotation, shift and mixing arithmetic seen in hashing or cipher code, which cryptominers use heavily. These include ADD ROR (+0.009589), MOV ROL (+0.006810), MOVZX ROL (+0.005942), BSWAP LEA (+0.004680), SHL XCHG (+0.004820), ADC XOR (+0.004860) and SUB SBB (+0.008168). The other high-ranked n-grams are generic control-flow and stack-handling sequences: POP CALL (+0.009302), PUSH RET (+0.007143), CALL RET (+0.006343), POP PUSH (+0.005764), POP LEA (+0.006383), ADD PUSH (+0.009150) and DEC PUSH (+0.007733). These are common in ordinary compiled code and could reflect packing, obfuscation, or simply typical function prologues and epilogues. Rotation and carry arithmetic also appears in legitimate cryptography, compression and checksum code, so these n-grams alone cannot confirm mining behavior. The model score supports suspicion, but the evidence provided cannot attribute the binary to cryptojacking specifically. It is therefore classed as low-confidence, with a suspicious but inconclusive profile.
